attempts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.

Image 1 is the authoritative character, costume, proportions and painted art style. Image 2 is ONLY the reference for the back-first slam posture and force direction; do not copy its human characters, costume, scenery or effects.

Repose the exact tiger martial artist from image 1 at the CONTACT moment of a rightward back slam. His chest, muzzle and gaze face SCREEN-LEFT, while his broad upper BACK and shoulder blade drive SCREEN-RIGHT into an imaginary opponent. This is a backward body-check with the BACK, not a forward crouching tackle. Rotate his whole torso and pelvis away from the original right-facing stance so the brown jacket's back is clearly visible on the right side of his body. Twist and lean the upper body slightly toward the left while pushing the rounded upper back forcefully right; the shoulder blade/back is the leading striking surface to the right, and the head and both forearms stay in front on the LEFT side of the torso. Bend both knees in a wide stable grounded stance, plant both feet on one level baseline, compress the supporting legs to deliver weight through the hips. The nearer arm is bent and raised toward the left; the other forearm bends in front toward the left. Do not extend a fist, elbow, foot or face toward the right as the attack point. Keep the back silhouette unobstructed and visibly braced for impact. Tail may trail behind the lower back but must not obscure the upper back contact surface.

Preserve the exact stocky short-limbed middle-aged orange tiger identity, large head/body proportions, sleepy half-lidded eye, ivory cheek fur, orange stripes, worn brown OPEN short jacket, ivory crossed robe underneath, brown sash, dark cropped trousers, wrist and ankle wraps, bare tiger paws. Preserve smooth ink contours, fine fur shapes and restrained painted shading, no pixel-art conversion and no redesign.

Output ONE assembled character only, no opponent, no impact burst, speed lines, motion ghosts, shadow, scenery, text or labels. Genuine RGBA transparent background. Use the same 1199x1312 portrait canvas and same character scale as image 1: crouching should lower the head rather than shrink the entire character. Keep the feet near the original baseline y1280, with all ears, hands, tail and feet visible and transparent margins.
